headline: Rates Edge Up After Last Week's Big Bond Rally
tileReason: The daily 30-year average ticked up to about 7.37% Friday as oil hit a five-month high, but this morning oil is easing and Fed hike bets are fading.
takeaway: After Thursday's sharp drop, the daily 30-year average gave a little back on Friday, rising 0.04% to 7.37% as oil prices settled at their highest since May. It was still a much better week than the one before. This morning the 10-year Treasury yield is roughly where it closed Friday, near 5.09%, and oil is falling after the U.S. eased sanctions on Russian energy, so lenders are likely to price close to Friday. Traders now see only about a 1-in-7 chance of a Fed hike on October 28. Over the next month, the odds lean slightly toward steady or lower rates, but hot inflation keeps higher rates very much in play.

fedOdds.title: Odds of a Fed hike on Oct 28
fedOdds.source: CME FedWatch via Benzinga (Oct 19, 8:23 AM ET) and PredictionMarketsPicks (Oct 19, 7:00 AM ET); Kalshi/Polymarket via PredictionMarketsPicks
fedOdds.note: CME FedWatch shows about 14% to 15%; prediction markets show 12% to 13%. Reports of Wednesday's post-CPI peak range from 44% to 54%. Kalshi still puts a December hike near 83%.

drivers.title: Bonds gave back a little of Thursday's rally
drivers.text: After Thursday's big rush into Treasury bonds, Friday was calmer. The 10-year Treasury yield ended roughly flat to slightly higher, near 5.09% to 5.12% depending on the source, and lenders nudged rates up a bit. The daily 30-year average rose 0.04% to 7.37%. Even so, the 10-year finished the week about 0.14% lower, its best week in a while.

drivers.title: Oil eases after U.S. relaxes Russia sanctions
drivers.text: Oil settled Friday at its highest level since May, which added to Friday's small rise in rates. Over the weekend markets digested President Trump's order waiving key sanctions on Russian energy, which could let more Russian fuel reach world markets. Brent crude fell about 2% to near $108 a barrel this morning. Cheaper energy eases inflation worries, which helps bond prices and nudges rates down.

drivers.title: Fed hike bets keep fading
drivers.text: CME FedWatch now puts the odds of an October 28 hike at roughly 15%, down from about half right after last Wednesday's inflation report. Fed officials are in their quiet period before the meeting, so no new speeches are expected to shake that. Fewer expected hikes take some upward pressure off longer-term rates.

drivers.title: Inflation is still running hot
drivers.text: September's consumer and wholesale price reports both came in above forecasts. Treasury Secretary Bessent blamed an energy shock tied to the Iran conflict and said prices should ease once it passes, but bond investors still want extra yield while inflation stays high, and markets expect a December hike. That keeps a floor under mortgage rates.

drivers.title: Tech stocks bounce, trimming safe-haven demand
drivers.text: AI and tech shares are recovering this morning after their worst week since June. When stocks calm down, some of the money that rushed into bonds can flow back out, which limits further drops in yields.

outlook.basis: I lean slightly toward steady or lower, but it's close. The gap between mortgage rates and the 10-year Treasury is still wider than usual (about 2.2% vs. a typical 2.0%), so rates can improve even if Treasury yields just hold steady. Oil is easing and October hike odds have dropped to about 15%. Against that, inflation keeps coming in hot, a December hike is still widely expected, and last week's bond rally was partly driven by stock-market fear, which can fade as stocks recover. The October 28 Fed decision, the October 29 inflation (PCE) data and the November 6 jobs report are the big swing events.
outlook.caveat: This is professional judgment from 30+ years watching these markets, not a guarantee. One oil headline or data surprise can move rates a quarter point in a day.

talkingPoints.buyers: The daily 30-year average is about 7.37%, still below the 7.5% range from two weeks ago. With hot inflation and a Fed meeting on October 28, it's worth asking your lender how a lock, a float-down option, or a short wait would each fit your closing date.
talkingPoints.sellers: Rates in the low-to-mid 7% range still stretch buyers' budgets. Realistic pricing, or a seller credit buyers can use to buy down their rate, can help your home stand out.
talkingPoints.oneLiner: Rates ticked up to about 7.37% Friday after a big drop, and with oil easing and Fed hike odds fading, this week starts on steadier footing.
